notes: Sweet, smokey and delicious.
Smokey with some ginger spice. I appreciate the added complexity.
Yummy huckleberry goodness.
Orange creamsicle ftw. Very yummy.
Lots of gin and then some slight sweetness from the Cocchi Rosa and the rhubarb bitters.
Herbal with some spice notes. Scent of vanilla, notable chartreuse on the mid palate with Carpano on the finish.
Lots of hogo with substantial sweetness.
Awesome fall cocktail. Lots of spice and a little sweetness.
Serious anise flavors with some sweetness.
Smoky & citrus
Really interesting combination with some unpleasant flavors on the finish.
Had it with Suze
Nine-Ten version is aged in barrels and uses Bols Genever instead of gin.
Not the best Sazerac I've had, but decent.
Rye is obvious, but mellow. Some sweetness and hints of fernet on the swallow.
The most drinkable fernet cocktail.
Wondering if they blended the lemon. Suspect use of simple syrup as well
Lots of tart citrus and floral violet flavors. I tried this with egg white for the first time...adds a nice element I hadn't tried before.
With St George Dry Rye gin
A little extra sweet compared to versions I've tried before, but still nice.
Sweet, like a fig newton.
Pleasant, botanical, and minty. Very nice!
Reminiscent of a boulevardier made with an apple brandy, though clearly has rye as well. The ice cube is bad ass.
Blueberries and botanicals with a lot of lemony aromas.
Lots of rum hogoness.
With St. George Aqua Libre rum. Very yummy.
Clear sherry taste but not overpowering. Quite nice.
Nice masala herbalness with a clear sour component.
Strong beet flavor with nice vegetal flavors and a nice spice.
Love it when made with Ransom.
Yummy as usual. Base was James E. Pepper 1776 Rye.
Made with St. George Agua Libre. Excellent!
Slightly spicy with some vinegar notes. One of the best on the summer menu.
Nice and simple. Light bourbon sweetness with some maple notes
A little sweet, but nice. Prefer the trader Vic version.
Did not recognize the Calvados initially. Rye & calvados are a nice combination.
Aromas of lavender and berries. Drink is sweet and reminds me of raspberries. Slight genever note on the finish.
Herbal with some initial sweetness. Almost like apple cider but with less apple flavors.
Lemonade and basil are prominent. Very subtle indications of other botanicals.
Bourbon, but lighter with some hints apple spices. Nice.
A sweet gimlet drink. Not sure I get nettle.
Bacon flavor is noticeable not overpowering
Nice tiki drink with coconut notes
Interesting and unusual presentation.
Alfalfa in the bottom was a little wild. Otherwise, a little too much unpeated scotch for me.
Not sure why Martini is the default vermouth, but quite good.
Don't really notice the whiskey or port reduction. Blood orange is strong and sweet.
The flavors of hogo and grape marry surprisingly well, making this a pleasantly complex drink. The port evaporation keeps the drink from being too alcoholic.
Very theatrical presentation. Makes me think of a "white" Sazerac, analogous to most white negronis that I've tried.
"Rested", meaning bottle-aged for 6 months. Very nice, though accidentally garnished with orange instead of lemon.
Strawberries and citrus. Faint hints of balsamic in the aftertaste. Nice, but perhaps a touch sweet for me.
Apples and allspice in the glass, with lots of allspice on the nose.
St George rum
Colonel E.H. Taylor
Much improved with the new formulation
Black Maple Hill
Smokey with a dark fruit body and some muted bitterness. Possibly could use a citrus garnish.
Botanicals, sweetness, and some citrus. The lime contributes a lot to the drink.
Nice Negroni variation. Less bitterness with a uniquely different flavor.
Limey fir with hints of gin botanicals. Mellow.
Citrus, tropical flavors with not too much sweetness. A nice tiki-style cocktail.
Citrusy, but with tastes of smoke. Like Mezcal but not.
Flamed orange up front with some cherry flavors. Agave spirit notes on the finish.
Not what I expected. Reminds me strongly of oatmeal with an orange finish
I didn't expect it to be clear. Smoky and a bit sweet for me. Grapefruit slightly noticeable.
Boozy but yum. Whiskey tempered by floral flavors and a touch of sweetness. Slight minty finish.
Mellow... Slightly sweet fruit flavors. Citrus barely noticeable, and only from the garnish. I wonder what this would be like with Armangac.
Lot of juice, not a lot of alcohol.
Sweet and slightly bitter. Wonder if it should have an orange peel instead...possibly flamed.
Apples, smoke and some citrus. Very nice.
Too much lime in this one, I think. Will need to try again.
First heard about at Haddington's in Austin. Sweet with a thicker mouthfeel, but the fernet keeps things balanced with some minty menthol flavors. Pretty good fernet cocktail.
Light, slightly sweet, a little bit of fruit.
Might as well be called suze and soda, though I'm sure the wine smoothes it out.
Dry, touch of Mezcal but not strong. Slight mint on the finish.
Very complex and interesting. Grassy, herbal, slightly smoky and packs a big punch.
Very interesting. Caraway and sherry flavors combine with citrus in a pleasing way.
Coffee initially, but absinthe presence becomes more noticeable.
Lots of juniper and botanicals. Slightly sweet with muted bitter flavors.
Smokey & sweet!
Sweetness of berries, followed by sherry flavor that lingers with slight bitterness.
Sweet with strong aromas of bananas coming from the garnish.
Pea pod and Aperol are noticeable. Long sweet finish.
Refreshing with a strong flavor of the terroir gin.
Nice and refreshing with an herbal note.
Dry and slightly floral. Unpeated whiskey apparent but not overpowering.
Sweet and smoky.
Very nice fernet cocktail.
Smokey, slightly spicy and refreshing.
Nice...smokey but citrusy and light.
Cache's Bloody Mary mix is great!
My favorite flip.
They use a nice peated scotch here.
Oak aged here at the hopping pig. Very nice.
This drink is still the best sage drink ever.
Got this from Raymond at Singlebarrel. His version looked like an old fashioned but much lighter in flavor with strong peach flavors mid-palate and some spice in the aftertaste.
Lots of hogo and citrus. Yum.
Nice, sweetish with slight complexity.
Opens with cucumber, becomes sweet with floral and botanical notes. Longish aftertaste possibly with slight hint of salt.
Cucumber on the nose, with a mixture of citrus, malt, and mint on the palate.
A bit too sweet. Probably less Zwack, and perhaps less sweet vermouth as well.
A little sweet, but nice rye spice and saffron notes.
Bitter with a nice mix of berry and woody flavors.
Very nice. Light and balanced with hints of sloe berries.
Quite pleasant and well balanced. Slight spicyness to go with the Mezcal smoke.
Anise aroma, very little on the open but moves to bitter sweet on the finish. Sweetness lingers but fades to slight bitter. Perhaps a different gin would help with the wateriness of the open?
Had this with the Kina Avion instead of Lillet. Quite nice, but again fairly thick and a little bit sweeter than I believe the drink is with Cocchi or Lillet.

Tonight with the Tempus Fugit spirits Kina Avion in place of the Lillet. Seems the accentuate the citrus flavors, making the drink a little more sour and thick. Not unpleasant, but I suspect this is not its best use.
Herbal manhattan. Chartreuse and punt e mes are very noticeable, but still has the properties of a typical manhattan.
Nice...very much like a manhattan.
Very balanced drink. Smokey Mezcal combined with a well crafted sour.
Nice mix of tequila and sweet vermouth flavors with maple notes on the finish.

0.5 oz creme de mure and 1 oz lemon juice this time. Less sweet, but the citrus is stronger and the smoke was reduced. Perhaps more whiskey and maybe less lemon. Next time: 0.25 creme de mure, 0.75 lemon, 1 laphroaig
Sweet but not half bad.
Scent of lime, sweet but not too much, with a slightly herbal finish.
Serious bitterness. Tastes like the pith of a citrus fruit.
Aromas of citrus and smoke. Absinthe & citrus flavor with a finish that incorporates first the absinthe and then the smoke. You would have to like absinthe to drink this, but quite nice if you do.
Dark fruit with a touch of anis on the nose, more dark fruit on the palate with a short anis finish. Very interesting absinthe cocktail.
Zafra on the open, but bitterness enters mid-palate and continues into the finish.
Fantastic!
Nicely based sour with a hint of Mezcal.
Very nice. Citrus but strong.
Nice sour variation...would make it myself at home.
Light for a bourbon drink. Slight bourbon on the open, Aperol in the middle, with slight bitterness on the finish. Might be good for a new bourbon drinker that likes negronis.
An anise sour with soda water. Good!
Milk & Honey apparently adds a little sweet vermouth, but I'm not sure this one did. Nice grapey addition to a rob roy.
Sweet with some whiskey notes on the finish.
Huge scent of caraway, sip has anise and sour flavors, finishes bitter-sweet.
Heavy on the terroir, but very nice.
Mezcal + grapefruit == win
Sweet and strong peach taste.
Aroma is primarily lemon citrus. Sip has some citrus and apple notes. Swallow has baked apples, some citrus, and slight sherry at the finish. Apple taste lingers pleasantly.
Manhattan variation. Some fernet and orange notes, but lots of bourbon throughout. Slightly tannic finish.
Big nose of angostura (duh). Citrus forward, with angostura notes on the finish, which is long.
Rye on the open, fruity finish.
Sloe flavor with some slight rye spice on the finish.
Refreshing with a nice mix of the honey, ginger and amaro flavors. Would make it myself at home.
Very peppery.
Interesting flavor mix. Very balanced. Hints of fernet at the front, fruit and rum in the middle, with the hint of fernet mint on the finish.
Fantastic!
Used Fee brothers gin-aged orange bitters instead. Quality drink.

Didn't have a grapefruit, so used an orange. Nice drink, with bitter, sweet, and smokey mezcal elements. The citron sausage liqueur has a surprisingly bitter element that will be fun to play with in the future.
On tap at Neighborhood.
Very interesting combination of many flavors. Would definitely make this again.
Relatively little maraschino flavor, despite the large pour. Lemon citrus notes are pleasant with the botanicals and slightly bitter finish.
Sweet with a touch of bitterness.
Much better with Ransom!
Sweet opening, bitter on the palate, with a moderately long cherry finish. A good negroni variation to keep in mind.
Better than the white negroni
Miranda made it with a little less coffee liqueur tonight. Much better and more negroni-ish

Hogo aroma with a hint of orange. Grass and citrus in the sip, some orange in the swallow with a quick finish. Very tiki. I don't notice any presence of alcohol despite the strong arrack, though I'm not a good judge of that.
Recipes online differ a bit in terms of the bitters used. Orange and ango is what I was told by Evan at The Lions Share who made it. Most online sources have a mix of orange bitters.
Made for me by Hass at The Lion's Share. Refreshing with a spicy kick. Need to get a bottle of these bitters.
Strong sherry flavors. Amaro on the open and mid palate. Finish is mainly sherry with some cocchi. One of the most unusual cocktails that I've had.
Sweet with a slightly bitter orangey finish. Can't really taste the agave, but still very nice.
At a Disney hotel bar.  Pretty sure they don't have bitters, or there just weren't any bitters in it.
Orange aroma, sweet open getting progressively bitter, finishing with a brandied cherry flavor.
Yeasty with genever on the palate and a mildly bitter finish. Orange twist instead of grapefruit in this one, and suspect grapefruit would be a bit better.
Bitter but light pleasant. Worth figuring out and making again.
Nicely balanced. Need to figure out which champagne they use.
Very nice drink. Opens sweet and light, finishes with a strong herbal Chartreuse note. A bit of burn on the finish...I wonder what it be like with yellow chartreuse instead of green.
Apple, spice, and pretty light.
Really cool drink. Benedictine sweetness initially, amaro in the middle and subtle smoky Mezcal notes on the finish. A good choice for the Mezcal initiate who likes bitter drinks like the 1794.
Sweet, hint of apple. Nice and refreshing. Good first drink of the night on my first visit to Little Branch.
A lot of citrus, some rye flavors on the finish. For me, a stronger rye would be better. Should try regular with a less whiskey-inclined drinker.
